properties.name: A software part's cost growth is MEASURED, by counting its work at three or more sizes, and budgeted at the size the design expects; a declared Big O alone is not taken as true
properties.statement: Where a software design says how a part's cost (work, memory, reply size or time) grows with the size of what it handles, the claim is checked: a verification counts the part's work (operations, store reads, bytes) at three or more sizes, never by a timer alone, fits the growth, and passes only when the fit is within the stated growth; and the part carries a budget at the size the design actually expects (e.g. "at 5,600 nodes, answers in 2 s"), which catches the constants and cliffs a growth class hides. A growth stated with no such check reads as a claim, not a measurement. Kept as intent by Anthony 2026-10-27 ("Let's go with your recommendations"): options (b)+(c) of the Big O brainstorm; (a) declared-only and the rest stay considered.
